name: EDGAR document-demand intensity / acquisition shock

source.official_dataset: SEC EDGAR Log File Data Sets
source.clock: request timestamps in log data must be reconciled to SEC filing acceptance/public boundary; no same-session use unless independently proven

new_source_findings: SEC confirms the modern log set begins 2020-05-19 and ends 2025-06-30.
SEC explicitly states the 2017-07-01 to 2020-05-18 interval is no longer available.
Modern and legacy schemas differ; SEC states the modern set omits some variables and excludes SEC-IP-originated searches.
SEC fair-access documentation separately distinguishes filing acceptance/dissemination timing from archive/index timing.
Bounded live archive probes found within-window request-time field-name drift: 2020-05-19 uses _time while 2022-12-30 and 2025-06-30 use time; normalization must be per-file and frozen.
negative_evidence: No defensible continuous 2003-2025 demand panel exists from the official logs because the 2017-2020 interval is unavailable.
A silent splice of legacy and modern schemas is prohibited.
Observed requests are not a direct measure of latent investor information demand; automated/bulk traffic and SEC-originated traffic require deterministic contamination handling.
The source page does not establish that post-2025-06-30 logs are publicly available in the same dataset contract.
next_gate: schema-variant normalization + request-quality contamination bounds + filing-acceptance/public-boundary join + mutation/PIT checks + independent reproduction
cheap_falsifiers: historical-window mutation changes a closed demand window
accession/CIK recovery is not deterministic from the logged URI schema
traffic-quality contamination cannot be bounded from available fields
request timestamps cannot be safely aligned after the filing public boundary
demand state collapses mechanically to generic attention or filing complexity

schema_drift.rule: Treat request-time field name as a schema-version attribute; normalize only after preserving the raw field name and source fingerprint.
